answer: A proof-of-uniqueness stake gate: before an AI agent can earn, it must post a stake the protocol slashes to zero when duplicate identities are detected. One identity per verified root is allowed, and each new agent acts as a mirror probe: when two accounts share a root the contract cannot tell which is real, so both stakes burn. A Sybil farm therefore needs a costly fresh root per clone, and one detection destroys the cluster's capital. The registry also acts as a bridge to reputation, so a defaulter cannot forge standing elsewhere. Forging ten thousand clones burns ten thousand stakes.
